subject: geography

moments.title: Rio Earth Summit (UNCED)
moments.who: 172 governments, 108 heads of state, around 17,000 NGO participants
moments.body: 3-14 June 1992: the UN Conference on Environment and Development in Rio de Janeiro produces the Rio Declaration on Environment and Development, Agenda 21 (a non-binding action plan), and opens for signature the UN Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) and Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD).
moments.takeaway: Rio was the largest intergovernmental meeting to that date. It institutionalised the Brundtland sustainable-development framework in international law.

moments.title: Conventions take effect
moments.body: UNFCCC enters force 1994; first COP held in Berlin 1995. CBD enters force 1993. The UN Convention to Combat Desertification follows in 1994. Agenda 21 inspires Local Agenda 21 programmes in thousands of municipalities.
moments.takeaway: Conventions agreed at Rio became the architecture for three decades of multilateral environmental negotiation.

now.title: From Rio to now
now.body: Rio+10 (Johannesburg 2002), Rio+20 (2012) and the 2015 SDGs all build on the 1992 framework. The Kyoto Protocol (1997) and Paris Agreement (2015) are downstream of the UNFCCC. The Aichi biodiversity targets (2010) and the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (2022) descend from the CBD.
now.open_questions: Has the Rio architecture delivered? Climate emissions have risen since 1992; biodiversity has declined. Defenders argue the institutions limit how bad it might otherwise be; critics that they enable continued damage with the appearance of action.

reflection: Rio set the framework that 30 years of environmental diplomacy has worked within. Whether that framework is part of the problem or part of the solution is one of the defining questions of contemporary environmental politics.
